compiled_state.title: As a developer, contracts/review-defenses.md pins the arbiter sub-schema to BLOCK/DEFER/DROP and retires the old SUSTAIN/ACCEPT/DOWNGRADE fields
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Story

As a developer, `contracts/review-defenses.md` is updated to pin the arbiter sub-schema to BLOCK/DEFER/DROP rulings and explicitly retire the old SUSTAIN/ACCEPT/DOWNGRADE fields, so that downstream consumers have a single authoritative schema reference.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] `contracts/review-defenses.md` arbiter sub-section updated: ruling enum is exactly `["BLOCK", "DEFER", "DROP"]`; old enum values `SUSTAIN`, `ACCEPT`, `DOWNGRADE` are listed as retired with a migration note
- [ ] Schema change is marked with a `schema_version` bump matching the cycle-ledger convention (from S2)
- [ ] Retired fields section explains what each old ruling mapped to in the new schema (e.g., SUSTAIN → DEFER, ACCEPT → DROP with resolution, DOWNGRADE → DEFER with severity adjustment)
- [ ] At least one other consumer doc or code file that references the contracts doc is updated to reflect the new schema (e.g., `REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md`, arbiter agent file)
- [ ] No references to old enum values remain in contracts doc outside of the explicit "retired fields" section

## Considerations

- [Ordering] Must complete before S5 (defense store) which writes records conforming to this schema
- [Migration clarity] The mapping from old → new enum is important for CI tools that may still emit old values; document the transition period policy (e.g., "old values rejected after version X")
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked
